subject: AeroPay performance: capacity safeguards & onboarding plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sam Andrews <sam.andrews@aeropay.com>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@aeropay.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: performance targets & burst behavior (recap + asks)

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on the big picture. Quick recap and a short list of asks so engineering can start sizing: 

Summary of AeroPay requirements as I understand them:
- Typical steady-state: ~400 concurrent requests (mostly short text inputs, avg token output ~40).
- Burst profile: up to ~1,200 concurrent requests for 2-4 minutes during settlement windows (~2x–3x of steady).
- Streaming: ~70% of requests will use streaming (token-at-a-time UX).
- Latency targets: 95th pct <= 350ms for non-streaming short prompts; for streaming we need first token <= 150ms and steady-state per-token <= 60ms.
- Tail considerations: a small subset (~5%) are long-context synthesis requests and are latency-tolerant but throughput-heavy.

Key asks from our side to finalize a POC plan: 
1) Can you share a 48‑hour traffic sample (time-series of qps and percent streaming) and one example request payload for both short and long-context flows?
2) Confirm whether the burst window is predictable (scheduled) vs purely spiky. You indicated it’s mostly scheduled around batch settlement — please confirm the usual clock and timezone.
3) Any compliance constraints (data residency, KMS) that would push you to Private deployment vs Dedicated?

Next technical / ops items we propose: 
- Warm pool strategy: we suggest a warm pool that keeps a subset of backends primed for <30s activation; need to confirm acceptable warmup time and warm pool size.
- Fallback SLO: define an acceptable degraded response (e.g., lower-quality quantized model) for brief overloads.

I attached a draft SLO matrix and a mutual action plan to this thread (aeropay-slo-matrix.xlsx, aeropay-mutual-action-plan.docx). If you can get us the traffic sample + one payload by end of day Friday we’ll produce a sizing recommendation and cost estimate for a 2-week POC.

Best,
Jonas

Thanks Jonas — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Burst is largely scheduled around nightly settlement (US/Eastern, 01:30–01:40 local). We sometimes see an unscheduled spike (~10% of windows) when downstream partners retry.
- We’ll drop a 48‑hour qps + streaming flag sample into a shared S3 link by Thursday EOD.
- Regarding warmup: our ops team really needs first-response latency back to production levels within ~45s of a surge start. 30s would be ideal but 45s is still workable.
- Compliance: for this POC we can run on Dedicated capacity in your hosted offering (no Private needed), but production may require a VPC next year.
- Cost question: can you give a delta estimate between a small dedicated warm pool vs nothing? We want ballpark numbers to justify the POC to finance.

One more: for streaming behavior we need stable ordering guarantees for token streams (we can share the UX flow).

Sam

Marissa / Ben — forwarding the AeroPay recap. Two things I want to highlight for commercial + product engineering: 

1) AeroPay is asking for a warmup expectation of ~30–45s to return to production latencies during their scheduled settlement windows. They’re willing to do a short Dedicated POC.
2) They want a rough delta cost for a small dedicated warm pool vs no warm pool to present to finance.

My read: this is mid-market account, good expansion potential. If we can offer a 4‑week dedicated POC (reserved minimal warm pool) with a modest discount and clear rollback option, we should be able to convert. They care about streaming first-token latency and ordered token streaming.

Action items: 
- Ben: can you prepare a commercial sketch (3 options: no warm pool, small warm pool, larger warm pool) by EOD Thu?
- Marissa: can you confirm from Eng whether a 50‑GPU warm pool is a reasonable starting point for their burst profile (we’ll refine after they share the 48h sample)? If not, propose an alternate warmup sizing and expected ramp time.

Jonas

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the clear summary. Quick replies to your asks: 

- Engineering sizing: 50 GPUs as a warm pool is high-level reasonable based on the numbers you sent on the call, but we should treat that as a starting estimate. That sizing assumes: 1) a mix of A100/compute-optimized instances, 2) continuous KV cache priming on a subset, and 3) model quantization profile for short prompts. Expected time to bring warm pool-backed endpoints to steady serving latency is ~20–40s depending on model and KV cache hit rate.

- Fallback model policy: we should plan an automatic fallback to a smaller-quantized model for the first 3 minutes of an excess burst window; that preserves availability and reduces tail latency. We’ll need AeroPay signoff on acceptable quality delta.

- Commercial: Ben, please prepare three options for the customer: 
   A) POC — 2 weeks Dedicated (no warm pool) — low cost, limited SLA
   B) POC — 2 weeks Dedicated + small warm pool (50 GPU-hour budget) — medium cost, short SLA window
   C) Pilot — 4 weeks Dedicated + reserved warm pool + prioritized routing — enterprise pricing, standard SLA

I’ve attached the mutual action plan draft. Jonas — once we get AeroPay’s 48h telemetry we can run a quick simulation and refine GPU-hour estimates.

Marissa Cole
